0.long_answer: The prophylactic injection used to prevent an immune cause of hydrops fetalis is the anti-D immunoglobulin injection. This injection is given to RhD-negative mothers who have not yet been sensitized to the Rh antigen, thereby preventing the maternal immune system from forming antibodies against fetal Rh-positive red blood cells. By blocking the maternal immune response, anti-D prophylaxis helps to prevent hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), which can lead to complications such as fetal anemia and hydrops fetalis in subsequent pregnancies.
